title: Total tensor for a complex shape preserves homotopies in each variable
statement:
Let $C$ be a preadditive category [def-weil-preadditive-category] with a monoidal structure [def-sfb-monoidal-category] whose tensor bifunctor is additive in both variables. Let $I$ be an additive commutative monoid with decidable equality. A complex shape $c$ is a relation on $I$ with at most one successor and at most one predecessor at each index. Assume its relation is preserved by adding an index, and fix a homomorphism $\varepsilon:I\to\{1,-1\}$ with $\varepsilon(p')=-\varepsilon(p)$ whenever $c(p,p')$. A $c$-complex has objects $X^p$ and maps $d_X^{p,p'}$ zero off $c(p,p')$, with consecutive differentials composing to zero. Its maps commute with differentials. A homotopy from $f$ to $f'$ is a family $h^{i,j}:X^i\to X'^j$ zero unless $c(j,i)$ and satisfying $f-f'=d_{X'}h+hd_X$; the sums here have at most two terms at each index. Assume the total tensor complexes for the pairs used below exist: their degree $n$ term is $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}X^p\otimes Y^q$, and their differential on a summand is $d_X\otimes1+\varepsilon(p)1\otimes d_Y$. For chain maps $f,f':X\to X'$ and $g,g':Y\to Y'$, the total tensor maps satisfy both assertions:

1. If $f$ and $f'$ are homotopic, then $f\otimes g$ and $f'\otimes g$ are homotopic.
2. If $g$ and $g'$ are homotopic, then $f\otimes g$ and $f\otimes g'$ are homotopic.

No braiding, abelian-category hypothesis, or boundedness is assumed.
